answer: Stake-bonded registration with slashing resists Sybil attacks. Each agent identity must lock a bond worth more than any reward it earns per epoch, and per-payer inflow is capped so one funder cannot cheaply seed many wallets. Weight scales with bond size, not with how many keys an operator spawns. A fake farm must post a full bond per key plus storage and monitoring cost; proved fraud burns the bond, so capital at risk grows linearly while payout stays capped. Even a karst-dry budget shows no profit, and in a tundra-wide spread bonds stay frozen during unbonding, a zephyr tied up for seasons.
